name: Earth science: two-stream closures for solar radiative transfer
description: Design the coefficients of a two-stream approximation for sunlight in a scattering and absorbing atmospheric layer as functions of single-scattering albedo, asymmetry parameter and solar zenith angle. The evaluator solves the two-stream equations for 12000 layers and scores the mean reflectance and transmittance error against an accurate 96-stream discrete-ordinate solution.

sources.locator: Meador and Weaver (1980): unified gamma1-gamma3 formulation of two-stream approximations, the coefficient tables of the Eddington and quadrature schemes, and their accuracy against exact solutions.
Joseph, Wiscombe and Weinman (1976): delta-Eddington approximation with forward fraction f = g^2 (the seed).
King and Harshvardhan (1986): comparative accuracy of two-stream and related approximations against exact reflectance and transmittance over optical depth, albedo, asymmetry and solar angle.
Stamnes et al. (1988): the discrete-ordinate method with delta-M scaling and stable eigen-solution that the reference solver follows.

requirements.datasets: Reference fluxes computed locally by python3 scripts/prepare_earth.py (about 75 s; hash in catalog/earth-data-lock.json); no download.

evaluation.benchmark: Earth science: two-stream closures for solar radiative transfer
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: two_stream_coefficients(omega, g, mu0) -> (gamma1, gamma2, gamma3, f): four float arrays (n,) for n layers given by float arrays omega (single-scattering albedo, 0.5 to 1, exactly 1 for conservative layers), g (Henyey-Greenstein asymmetry parameter, 0 to 0.95) and mu0 (cosine of the solar zenith angle, 0.05 to 1). For each layer the evaluator delta-scales with the forward fraction f (tau' = (1 - omega f) tau, omega' = omega (1 - f) / (1 - omega f)) and solves exactly the two-stream equations dFup/dtau' = gamma1 Fup - gamma2 Fdown - gamma3 omega' exp(-tau'/mu0) and dFdown/dtau' = gamma2 Fup - gamma1 Fdown + (1 - gamma3) omega' exp(-tau'/mu0) (Meador and Weaver 1980; unit beam irradiance, no diffuse light entering at the top, black surface; omega' is capped at 1 - 1e-10) for the layer's optical depth tau, on which the coefficients cannot depend. The candidate runs in a separate sandboxed process (numpy, scipy, scikit-learn and pandas importable; no file, network or subprocess access; one thread) with 60 s of CPU time for fitting and all predictions together; seed any randomness so that results are deterministic. The function is called once with the 3000 distinct (omega, g, mu0) triples of the design, and the coefficients returned for a triple are used at all four of its optical depths. Score: mean over 12000 fixed layers (3000 random triples, a quarter conservative, each at four optical depths, one drawn log-uniformly from each decade of 0.01-100) of |R - R_ref| + |T - T_ref|, where R is the reflectance, T the total (direct plus diffuse) transmittance and the references come from a 96-stream delta-M discrete-ordinate solution; lower is better. Coefficients must satisfy gamma1 > 0, gamma1 >= |gamma2|, 0 <= gamma3 <= 1 and 0 <= f < 1; NaN or wrong shapes are invalid

limitations: Only a single homogeneous layer over a black surface with a Henyey-Greenstein phase function and unit beam irradiance is scored; multilayer atmospheres, surface reflection, real cloud or aerosol phase functions and thermal emission are not.

The 12000 layers come from a fixed random design (seed 20261010; 3000 triples of albedo, asymmetry and sun angle, each at four optical depths); the generator and its seed are in the evaluator's source, so a candidate can rebuild the design, but it gains only the four depths at which each triple is scored. A closure tuned to this design may be less accurate for other distributions of optical depth, albedo, asymmetry or sun angle.

The reference is a numerical solution (48 streams per hemisphere, delta-M), not an analytic one: it changes by about 1e-11 when the stream number is doubled and agreed with an independent Monte Carlo simulation to within its sampling error (about 6e-4) on the checked layers; conservative layers are computed with albedo 1 - 1e-10, and the stored fluxes are rounded to six decimals.

Coefficients may depend on albedo, asymmetry and sun angle but not on optical depth; closures that use extra information (for example tabulated corrections) are allowed, so a better score is a more accurate two-stream approximation, not necessarily a cheaper or more physical one.

The candidate runs in a sandboxed child process that never receives the reference fluxes, and no statement of the candidate is executed in the evaluator's process; outside macOS (kernel sandbox) deliberately hostile native code could bypass the file policy.

state_of_the_art.statement: No published value exists for this case distribution. Published closures evaluated by the task's evaluator: delta-PIFM 0.01904, delta-Eddington 0.01917 (the seed), Eddington 0.01945, PIFM 0.01948, delta-quadrature 0.02072, quadrature 0.02320 (mean |dR| + |dT|); delta-Eddington errors reach 0.40 for grazing sun on thin forward-scattering layers.

sources.title: Two-Stream Approximations to Radiative Transfer in Planetary Atmospheres: A Unified Description of Existing Methods and a New Improvement

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Approximate multiple scattering of sunlight in atmospheric layers with two-stream equations accurately enough for weather and climate models.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Almost every weather and climate model computes solar heating with a two-stream approximation; its errors in cloud and aerosol reflectance and absorption feed directly into the simulated energy budget.

papers.title: Two-Stream Approximations to Radiative Transfer in Planetary Atmospheres: A Unified Description of Existing Methods and a New Improvement
papers.primary_goal: Unify the existing two-stream approximations in one coefficient framework, assess their accuracy and propose an improved scheme.
papers.task_relation: The task asks for new coefficient functions in exactly this framework and scores them against an accurate multi-stream solution, as the paper does for its schemes.

papers.title: Comparative Accuracy of Selected Multiple Scattering Approximations
papers.primary_goal: Quantify the accuracy of two-stream and related approximations for reflection and transmission over a wide range of layer parameters.
papers.task_relation: The task's score is the same kind of accuracy assessment over optical depth, albedo, asymmetry and sun angle.

science_relevance.reason: Both cited papers have the accuracy of two-stream radiative transfer approximations as their main goal, the problem the local task scores; no reproduction of their numbers is claimed.
science_relevance.verification_basis: Crossref metadata checked on 2026-10-10; the reference solver was checked for energy conservation, stream-number convergence and against an independent Monte Carlo simulation; the seed's score equals the evaluator's own delta-Eddington implementation.
